sources.description: Canonical QuakeWorld gamecode shipped with the original QW source release. Frozen baseline that every mod (KTX, clan-arena, freshteam, etc.) inherits from. Source files at research/repos/qwcl-original/QW/progs/.
sources.notes:
Engine-side constants (sv_maxspeed=320, friction=4, accelerate=10, stopspeed=100, edgefriction=2) live in the cvars table once each engine's extraction picks them up; not loaded into gameplay_mechanics.
Monster stat rows (kind=monster) cite the original Quake v1.06 QuakeC source release, acquired at /research/repos/QuakeC-releases/progs/ (mirror https://github.com/maddes-b/QuakeC-releases, branch id1-original, commit 85ccafd2652ec550a561849a6a5eb92e62cdc115, acquired 2026-06-12). This is the PRISTINE 1.06 release (no fixes applied); the SHA is the anchor since the repo's branches can be rebased. The 1.06 release is the competitive-QW monster baseline; the 2021 rerelease QC differs and is NOT used. Spot-verified at acquisition: shambler.qc health=600, ogre.qc health=200 (spec D1). Monster refs use the leading-slash citation form (plan D7); the id1 source_root below stays QW/progs/ unchanged.

This block is the canonical owner of the ktx gameplay_sources registry row (finding F3): the extractor-path loaders (load-gameplay-tables / -taxonomies / -modes) only ASSERT this row exists; this seed file is the sole writer of its display_name / description / source_root / notes. The hardcoded override rows below are the game-content-catalog arc's Phase 3 deliverable (2026-06-12); the bloodfest monster rows and the eight taxonomy kinds are written by the KTX onboarding extractor pipeline and are NOT in this file. source_root carries the leading slash by historical convention; the citation gate treats it as repo-root-relative (plan D7).

entities.name: backpack
entities.notes: 120s lifetime then auto-removed; pickup grants weapon + remaining ammo.

entities.name: green_armor
entities.notes: absorbs 30% of damage up to 100 armor.

entities.name: health_15_rotten
entities.notes: T_Heal with ignore=0 caps at max_health (default 100); items.qc:217 is the cap site, items.qc:220 is megahealth's separate ignore=1 path.

entities.name: megahealth_100
entities.notes: respawn_seconds=20 for the basic regen-after-pickup cycle; the megahealth-specific decay-then-regen sequence is separate (5s initial decay tick at items.qc:321, then -1 hp/s back to max, then 20s regen at items.qc:356).

entities.name: pentagram
entities.notes: invul absorbs all damage; 5-minute respawn.

entities.name: pickup_nailgun
entities.notes: weapon pickups exist on map only when deathmatch <= 3.

entities.name: quad_damage
entities.notes: dropped on death only when worldspawn key 'dq' is set. combat.qc:127 is the if(deathmatch==4) gate (the *8 path); combat.qc:130 is the default *4 multiply. The dq drop-on-death gate lives in PlayerDie at player.qc:552, not client.qc.

entities.name: red_armor
entities.notes: absorbs 80%.

entities.name: ring_of_shadows
entities.notes: 5-minute respawn. The dr drop-on-death gate lives in PlayerDie at player.qc:568, not client.qc.

entities.name: yellow_armor
entities.notes: absorbs 60%.

entities.name: monster_army
entities.notes: Grunt: 30 hp hitscan trooper. Fires a 4-pellet shotgun burst (16 max if all pellets connect) and drops a 5-shell backpack on death. Values cited into the v1.06 tree; wiki cross-check in phase-2-findings.md.

behaviors.name: drops_backpack_on_death
behaviors.value: 5 shells

behaviors.name: lead_shot_aim
behaviors.value: aims slightly behind the player's current position to punish straight-line dodging

entities.name: monster_boss
entities.notes: Chthon (boss): no depletable health -- immune to all weapon damage (DAMAGE_NO), killed only by the level's lightning terminals (1 hit on Easy, 3 otherwise). Throws lava balls that behave like rockets (100-120 direct + 120 splash, speed 300). Excluded from bloodfest. Wiki cross-check in phase-2-findings.md.

attacks.name: lavaball
attacks.damage: 100 + random() * 20 direct hit, plus T_RadiusDamage 120 splash (rocket-equivalent via T_MissileTouch)

behaviors.name: immune_to_player_weapons
behaviors.value: true -- self.takedamage = DAMAGE_NO; conventional weapon damage does nothing

behaviors.name: kill_mechanic_lightning_gate
behaviors.value: killed only by the map's lightning terminals; 1 hit on skill 0, 3 hits on skill 1-3

behaviors.name: fires_two_lavaballs_per_cycle
behaviors.value: true -- fires at attack frame 9 and frame 20 of each attack cycle

entities.name: monster_demon1
entities.notes: Fiend: 300 hp. A two-claw swipe (10-15 each) and a high-damage leap (40-50) that only hurts while moving fast. Wiki cross-check in phase-2-findings.md.

behaviors.name: leap_attack
behaviors.value: launches self at v_forward*600 + up 250; leap touch damage only lands when speed > 400

entities.name: monster_dog
entities.notes: Rottweiler: 25 hp fast melee. A standing bite plus a leap that deals extra contact damage only while moving fast. Wiki cross-check in phase-2-findings.md.

behaviors.name: leap_attack
behaviors.value: launches self at v_forward*300 + up 200; leap touch damage only lands when speed > 300

entities.name: monster_enforcer
entities.notes: Enforcer: 80 hp. Fires laser bolts (15 dmg, speed 600) in two-shot bursts and drops a 5-cell backpack. Wiki cross-check in phase-2-findings.md.

behaviors.name: drops_cells_on_death
behaviors.value: 5 cells

behaviors.name: two_shot_burst
behaviors.value: true -- fires on two attack frames (enf_atk6 and enf_atk10) per sequence

entities.name: monster_fish
entities.notes: Rotfish: 25 hp swimmer with a short-range bite (within 60 units). No gib path in vanilla Quake v1.06 -- gib_health is null. (quakewiki lists a -20 gib threshold, but that applies only to the Scourge of Armagon expansion, not vanilla; operator-confirmed keep-source 2026-06-12. See phase-2-findings.md.)

behaviors.name: no_gib_path
behaviors.value: no health-threshold gib in vanilla; death is a single f_death animation

entities.name: monster_hell_knight
entities.notes: Death Knight: 250 hp. Sword melee plus a 6-spike magic missile fan (9 dmg each, speed 300). The launch_spike helper default speed (1000) is overridden to 300. Wiki cross-check in phase-2-findings.md.

behaviors.name: spike_volley_count
behaviors.value: fires 6 magic spikes per ranged attack, fanned horizontally (offsets -2..3)

entities.name: monster_knight
entities.notes: Knight: 75 hp melee-only. One sword attack (the standing and running sequences share the same damage formula). No ranged attack -- its defining weakness. Wiki cross-check in phase-2-findings.md.

behaviors.name: attack_style_selection
behaviors.value: standing swing (knight_atk1) when enemy within 80 units, else a running charge-slash (knight_runatk1, ai_melee_side fight.qc:253); both deal identical sword damage

entities.name: monster_ogre
entities.notes: Ogre: 200 hp. Chainsaw melee plus a lobbed grenade (40 splash, speed 600) that arcs on a fixed +200 z-velocity. Drops a 2-rocket backpack. Wiki cross-check in phase-2-findings.md.

attacks.name: grenade_lob
attacks.damage: T_RadiusDamage 40 splash (max at center, falls off with distance)

behaviors.name: grenade_fixed_arc
behaviors.value: grenade z-velocity is hardcoded to +200 (cannot aim vertically)

behaviors.name: drops_backpack_on_death
behaviors.value: 2 rockets

entities.name: monster_oldone
entities.notes: Shub-Niggurath (boss): the nominal 40000 health is unreachable -- pain resets it to full, so she is immune to weapons and is killed only by telefrag. No attacks of her own. Excluded from bloodfest. Wiki cross-check in phase-2-findings.md.

behaviors.name: health_resets_on_pain
behaviors.value: true -- the nopain handler resets health to 40000 on every hit; immune to normal damage depletion

behaviors.name: kill_mechanic_telefrag
behaviors.value: killed only by telefrag (the player rides the level teleporter through Shub-Niggurath)

behaviors.name: no_attacks
behaviors.value: true -- Shub idles and never initiates combat; she has no attack functions

entities.name: monster_shalrath
entities.notes: Vore: 400 hp. Fires a single homing voreball (40 splash, launch speed 400, homing 250/350) that tracks the player. Wiki cross-check in phase-2-findings.md.

attacks.name: homing_missile
attacks.damage: T_RadiusDamage 40 splash (max at center, falls off with distance)

behaviors.name: homing_tracking
behaviors.value: launched at speed 400, then re-homes toward the enemy every 0.2s at speed 250 (350 on nightmare)

behaviors.name: zombie_bonus_damage
behaviors.value: deals an extra 110 direct damage if the missile hits a monster_zombie (gibs zombies)

entities.name: monster_shambler
entities.notes: Shambler: 600 hp, the toughest id1 monster. A smash and a claw melee plus a hitscan lightning beam that never misses in range. Takes only half damage from rocket/grenade splash and from the lightning gun (the combat.qc classname checks). Boss-able in bloodfest (see the ktx fact-family row). Wiki cross-check in phase-2-findings.md.

entities.name: monster_tarbaby
entities.notes: Spawn (blob): 80 hp kamikaze. Bounces itself at the player (jump touch 10-20 while moving fast) and detonates for 120 splash on death. No gib path. quakewiki has no stats page (Spawn disambiguation) -- no external cross-check; see phase-2-findings.md.

behaviors.name: kamikaze_death_explosion
behaviors.value: on death calls T_RadiusDamage 120 (then BecomeExplosion); no gib path

behaviors.name: touch_damage_requires_speed
behaviors.value: jump touch only deals damage when speed > 400

behaviors.name: no_pain_flinch
behaviors.value: true -- no th_pain assigned; the tarbaby never flinches

entities.name: monster_wizard
entities.notes: Scrag: 80 hp, the only flying id1 monster. Fires two acid spikes per attack (9 dmg each, speed 600; launch_spike default 1000 overridden to 600). Wiki cross-check in phase-2-findings.md.

behaviors.name: fires_two_spikes_per_attack
behaviors.value: true -- Wiz_StartFast spawns two offset fire entities that each launch one wizspike

entities.name: monster_zombie
entities.notes: Zombie: 60 hp pseudo-immortal. Throws flesh gibs (10 dmg, speed 600). Health resets to 60 on every pain frame, so the gib_health of 0 means it can only be killed by dealing 60+ damage in one frame (always gibs; no negative threshold). Wiki cross-check in phase-2-findings.md.

behaviors.name: health_resets_on_pain
behaviors.value: true -- zombie_pain resets health to 60 on every hit, so the zombie cannot be worn down by attrition

behaviors.name: only_killable_by_60_damage_in_one_frame
behaviors.value: true -- the only kill (always a gib) needs 60+ damage in a single frame (rockets, grenades, quad shotgun)

behaviors.name: knockdown_on_25_plus_damage
behaviors.value: true -- a hit of 25+ damage forces the long knockdown animation

entities.name: grenade
entities.notes: Bounces (MOVETYPE_BOUNCE), gravity-affected. The grenade has no separate direct-impact damage value, but a direct contact with a player (takedamage == DAMAGE_AIM) triggers GrenadeExplode immediately at weapons.qc:618, dealing the full 120 splash. So a grenade that hits you does hurt -- up to 120 -- via the explosion, not an impact value. The earlier source_ref weapons.qc:600 pointed at the T_RadiusDamage splash call (role-wrong for a direct-damage=0 claim); it is kept as splash_damage_source_ref where it belongs.

entities.name: rocket
entities.notes: direct damage is 100..120 random; splash flat 120.

entities.name: spike
entities.notes: nailgun projectile.

entities.name: super_spike
entities.notes: super-nailgun projectile.

entities.name: axe
entities.notes: 75 damage in deathmatch>3.

entities.name: grenade_launcher
entities.notes: direct hit deals 0 damage; explosion only.

entities.name: lightning_gun
entities.notes: in DM4+ discharge in water deals 4000 dmg (instakill).

entities.name: nailgun
entities.notes: damage realised on spike_touch. Refire timer is set inside W_FireSpikes at weapons.qc:759 (parallels SNG's weapons.qc:726 inside W_FireSuperSpikes); the player_nail1/player_nail2 frames at player.qc:190/203 also re-set attack_finished after each W_FireSpikes call. Citing the fire-function body for parity with SNG.

entities.name: rocket_launcher
entities.notes: damage is 100 + random()*20 = 100..120 effective.

entities.name: super_nailgun
entities.notes: shares spike-launcher with nailgun; damage realised on superspike_touch.

entities.name: backpack
entities.notes: Yawnmode throttles ammo transfer between players: a dropped backpack caps at 25 shells / 50 nails / 25 rockets / 25 cells (vanilla player ceilings 100/200/100/100), inside an `if (k_yawnmode)` block at items.c:2826. Additionally (items.c:2754) an idle dying player's pack is downgraded to a shotgun pack in dmm1. Mode-scoped.

props.dropped_weapon_downgrade: if the dying player was not recently shooting (dm1, attack_finished < time), the dropped pack is downgraded to a shotgun pack (no weapon transfer)

entities.name: green_armor
entities.notes: Yawnmode raises green-armor damage absorption 0.3 -> 0.4 (`type = (k_yawnmode ? 0.4 : 0.3)` at items.c:474). armor_absorb is a fractional protection coefficient, kept in props. Mode-scoped.

entities.name: monster_shambler
entities.notes: KTX removes the shambler's vanilla half-damage-from-lightning-beam: a shambler takes FULL lightning-gun beam damage in KTX (no shambler branch in LightningHit). Unconditional. The shambler's half-damage-from-EXPLOSIONS is still present (except in bloodfest -- see the bloodfest mechanic row). Health 600, gib -60, and melee/lightning damage are all faithful.

props.mechanism: KTX LightningHit (weapons.c:1101-1118) applies T_Damage at full value with no monster_shambler guard; vanilla halved LG-beam damage to shamblers

entities.name: monster_zombie
entities.notes: KTX randomizes the zombie gib-lob projectile speed to 600-700 per shot (`VectorScale(..., 600 + 100 * g_random(), ...)` at sp_zombie.c:616) where vanilla uses a fixed 600. Unconditional reimplementation; all other zombie stats (health 60, pain-reset, 60-damage gib, 25-knockdown) are faithful.

entities.name: rocket
entities.notes: KTX unconditionally fixes rocket direct-hit damage at 110, where vanilla is a uniform-random 100-120 (`damg = 110` at weapons.c:986, else-branch of the shambler check). The mean is unchanged (110); the divergence is the removal of the +-10 random variance ("rockets always do 110"). Gate {} (always -- the one weapon delta a normal-deathmatch player feels). Special case: 55 vs monster_shambler when not bloodfest (weapons.c:981). The boss lavaball uses the same T_MissileTouch line, so it inherits the 110.

props.also_applies_to: monster_boss lavaball (shared T_MissileTouch path, same weapons.c:986 line)

entities.name: rocket
entities.notes: In midair, a quad-carrying player's rockets fly at 2000 (vanilla 1000) and glow blue. Single-key gate {"mode":"midair"}; the quad requirement (super_damage_finished > time, weapons.c:1059) is the secondary condition in props. Mode-scoped.

entities.name: spike
entities.notes: Yawnmode accelerates fired nails (spikes) 1000 -> 1800 units/s (`VectorScale(dir, k_yawnmode ? 1800 : 1000, ...)` at weapons.c:1479). Affects both nailgun and super-nailgun spikes. Mode-scoped.

entities.name: super_spike
entities.notes: Yawnmode lowers super-nail (super_spike) damage 18 -> 16 per hit (`T_Damage(..., k_yawnmode ? 16 : 18)` at weapons.c:1625). Mode-scoped.

entities.name: axe
entities.notes: In dmm4+ (the `if (deathmatch > 3)` branch at weapons.c:122) KTX hardcodes axe damage to 75, where vanilla Quake axe is 20 in every mode. This is a KTX-specific deathmatch buff, not vanilla dmN behavior (id1_native=false). Gate {"dm":4} denotes "dmm4+"; the exact `> 3` condition is in props. This is a separate row from the dmm3-yawnmode axe=50 above (different gate).

entities.name: axe
entities.notes: Yawnmode raises axe damage 20 -> 50 (one-shots in dmm3). The assignment at weapons.c:128 (`damage = k_yawnmode ? 50 : 20`) sits INSIDE an `else if (deathmatch == 3)` branch (weapons.c:126) -- the delta requires yawnmode AND dm3, so dm3 is a real code gate recorded as the secondary condition in props per the single-key rule (D3, finding F10). Mode-scoped: with yawnmode off, the else-branch is the vanilla 20.

entities.name: super_shotgun
entities.notes: Yawnmode buffs the super-shotgun: 21 pellets (vanilla 14), a WIDER spread 0.18/0.12 (vanilla 0.14/0.08 -- the source comment says "larger SSG spread", correcting an earlier "tightened" mischaracterization), and a longer 0.8s reload (vanilla 0.7). pellet_count / spread / reload are not indexable columns, so they live in props with per-field source_refs. Mode-scoped.

mechanics.name: armor_absorb_formula
mechanics.notes: armor depletes first, then health takes the remainder.

mechanics.name: armor_pickup_upgrade_gate
mechanics.notes: Picking up armor only upgrades you if the new armor's protective product (type * value) exceeds your current one; otherwise the pickup is skipped and the item is NOT consumed. This is why walking over green armor while wearing red does nothing. On a successful pickup armortype and armorvalue are both overwritten (items.qc:406), not added.

mechanics.name: best_weapon_drops_lg_in_water
mechanics.notes: auto weapon-select (best-weapon) will not pick the lightning gun when the player is submerged (waterlevel > 1), to avoid the self-discharge; it falls through to the next best weapon.

mechanics.name: lg_direct_zvelocity_boost
mechanics.notes: a lightning-gun bolt hitting a player adds +400 to the target's z-velocity (a small upward pop); only applied when the struck entity is a player.

mechanics.name: lg_water_discharge_damage_per_cell
mechanics.notes: firing the LG underwater discharges all cells and deals 35*cells radius damage centered on the shooter -- the classic "LG in water kills you". Empties ammo_cells to 0.

props.dm4_variant_note: dm4 uses a fixed 4000 self-damage on a random low-roll branch (dm_mode_rules.dm4_rules.lg_water_self_damage); 35*cells is the base non-dm4 discharge

mechanics.name: rocket_jump_multiplier_default
mechanics.notes: rj=0 disables rocket jumping; rj=1 default; some servers set rj=2. The default of 1 is established by the global declaration `float rj = 1` at defs.qc:443; client.qc:517 is the conditional override gate that only fires when the server infokey rj is non-zero.

mechanics.name: self_splash_half_damage
mechanics.notes: The radius damage you take from your own rocket or grenade is half what an enemy at the same distance takes (combat.qc:278). This is the QC-side self-damage reduction that makes rocket-jumping survivable; the rj infokey knockback multiplier (constant rocket_jump_multiplier_default) is a separate scalar.

mechanics.name: splash_falloff_gradient
mechanics.notes: Radius damage is NOT flat. T_RadiusDamage delivers points = damage - 0.5*distance from the blast center; targets whose points come out non-positive simply take nothing (delivery is gated on points > 0 at combat.qc:279). NOTE the source order: the clamp at combat.qc:273-274 bounds the DISTANCE TERM before the subtraction (dead code in practice -- vlen is non-negative); it is NOT a delivered-damage clamp. The per-weapon splash_damage (e.g. RL 120) is the MAXIMUM at zero distance; delivered splash decreases linearly to the edge of the damage+40 radius. The "splash flat 120" wording on the rocket and grenade rows is the nominal max, not the value delivered at range.

props.beam_twin_note: T_BeamDamage (LG discharge) uses the same linear falloff (distance term combat.qc:309)

mechanics.name: ssg_last_shell_fires_shotgun
mechanics.notes: the super shotgun needs 2 shells; with exactly 1 shell left it fires a single-barrel shotgun shot instead of failing. Player-visible behavior on the last shell.

mechanics.name: sv_gravity_default
mechanics.notes: per-map override on e1m8 (boss fight). The cvar itself is tunable by the engine; this row captures the QC-side default set in worldspawn.

mechanics.name: timelimit_unit_minutes
mechanics.notes: the timelimit cvar is specified in MINUTES; StartFrame multiplies by 60 to get the internal seconds value. A server admin setting timelimit 10 means a 10-minute match.

mechanics.name: death_health_floor
mechanics.notes: on death the engine clamps health to -99 (combat.qc:66) so the status bar does not display extreme negative values. This is the hard floor any post-death health read sees.

mechanics.name: deathtype_enum
mechanics.notes: 7 deathtypes total. There is NO "ax" deathtype (axe uses axhitme boolean at defs.qc:516, set at weapons.qc:52). There is NO "grenade" deathtype (grenade explosion goes through T_RadiusDamage which assigns "rocket" downstream). "laser" exists in misc.qc:319 (laser-trap entities).

mechanics.name: exit_level_kill
mechanics.notes:
Distinct from telefrag despite the same 50000 damage. This is the rule
that kills you when you touch a trigger_changelevel brush on a server
with samelevel=2 (or samelevel=3 on non-start maps). Most servers running
single-player maps in QW deathmatch enable this so randos can't advance
the map mid-match. The obituary reads attacker.classname=='trigger_changelevel'
— same dispatch model as telefrag but different attacker class.

mechanics.name: friendly_fire_teamplay_0
mechanics.notes: free-for-all. combat.qc:199 is the teamplay==1 guard; when teamplay==0 no guard fires and execution falls through to the unconditional damage application at combat.qc:210.

mechanics.name: friendly_fire_teamplay_1
mechanics.notes: standard teamplay 1.

mechanics.name: friendly_fire_teamplay_2
mechanics.notes: teamkill costs 1 frag.

mechanics.name: friendly_fire_teamplay_3
mechanics.notes: similar to 1; specific QW variant.

mechanics.name: suicide_frag_penalty
mechanics.notes: the player 'kill' command (ClientKill) subtracts 2 frags ("extra penalty", client.qc:298). This is the explicit-suicide penalty; ordinary environmental or self-weapon deaths use the standard single-frag loss handled in the obituary path.

mechanics.name: telefrag
mechanics.notes:
Real telefrag: when a player teleports onto another player, an invisible
teledeath entity is spawned at the destination and deals 50000 damage to
whoever's standing there. Pent has a special interaction: the teledeath2
path at triggers.qc:343 routes the kill back to the would-be attacker
(Satan's-power-deflects message), costing them a frag. No deathtype string
is assigned; the obituary handler dispatches on attacker.classname.

mechanics.name: dm2_rules
mechanics.notes: Classic deathmatch mode 2 ("silly old rules", per the items.qc:328 comment). Every item-respawn timer -- health (items.qc:328), armor (items.qc:411), ammo and weapons (items.qc:868) -- schedules its respawn nextthink only when deathmatch != 2, so in dm2 the timer is never set and items do NOT respawn after pickup. The earlier "respawn_30s_ammo" wording was backwards: 30s is the NON-dm2 ammo respawn time.

mechanics.name: dm3_rules
mechanics.notes: half ammo respawn time. In dm3 (and dm5), picking up a backpack containing the grenade or rocket launcher tops your rockets up to a minimum of 5 (items.qc:1574) so you can always fire the weapon you just got.

mechanics.name: dm4_rules
mechanics.notes: DM4 OctaPower preset. The 255-ammo block is gated by the worldspawn 'axe' infokey. DM4-specific extras: picking up the quad strips your armor and cells (items.qc:47); item entities do not spawn at all (items.qc:891, each item think returns early); when the quad expires you snap back to cells=255 / armorvalue=1 / armortype=0.8 / health=100 (client.qc:1064); bonus pentagram lasts 30s (items.qc:1489); and firing a grenade costs the shooter 10 HP (weapons.qc:673).

loadout_axe_mode_on.notes: axe-mode DM4 inherits the same 250hp/200armor/3s-invul block but skips the 255-ammo + extra-weapons grant.

mechanics.name: dm5_rules
mechanics.notes: DM5 Quadmachine preset.

mechanics.name: crush_squish
mechanics.notes: damage value comes from the crushing entity (door/plat dmg field); often instakill if dmg unset. plats.qc:114 is the first concrete deathtype="squish" assignment; client.qc:1268 is the obituary-check site (where the deathtype string is read), not where it's set.

mechanics.name: drowning
mechanics.notes: 12s grace, then 1s ticks. self.dmg starts at 2 (initial water damage, client.qc:467), increments +2 each tick (client.qc:797), and when it exceeds 15 it resets to 10 (client.qc:799). So delivered damage climbs 4,6,8,10,12,14 then oscillates 10,12,14 -- the per-tick maximum is 14 and 10 is the post-overflow floor. The earlier single damage_source_ref pointed only at the increment line.

mechanics.name: fall_damage
mechanics.notes: flat 5 dmg above -650 velocity; water absorbs entirely.

mechanics.name: gib_threshold
mechanics.notes: When health drops below -40 the player explodes into gibs instead of ragdoll (player.qc:598; the obituary text switches to the gib variant at client.qc:1361). Lava deaths gib at a lower bar, health < -15 (client.qc:1452). Gib scatter velocity scales with overkill: VelocityForDamage multiplies the base by 0.7x above -50, 2x above -200, and 10x below -200 (player.qc:465-476); gibs persist 10-20s (player.qc:497). Lives in player.qc, not client.qc.

mechanics.name: lava
mechanics.notes: ticks 5x more often than slime; biosuit only slows ticks (does NOT block).

mechanics.name: slime
mechanics.notes: biosuit fully blocks slime damage.

mechanics.name: trigger_hurt
mechanics.notes:
Damage-dealing brush placed by the mapper. self.dmg is per-instance: a void brush
with dmg=1000 instakills, a low-damage hazard area at default dmg=5 is just
attrition. Unlike telefrag/exit_level_kill (50000 dmg), trigger_hurt damage goes
through normal T_Damage so armor and pent both apply. There is no QC handler for
engine-level out-of-world Z; instead, mappers put a trigger_hurt brush above the
engine's hard Z floor to catch players first. This is what kills you when you
jump into the void on most maps.

mechanics.name: bbox_max
mechanics.notes: VEC_HULL_MAX.

mechanics.name: bbox_min
mechanics.notes: VEC_HULL_MIN. Bounding box is engine-enforced.

mechanics.name: knockback_factor
mechanics.notes: knockback scales with damage. rj cvar multiplies self-damage knockback.

mechanics.name: max_health
mechanics.notes: clamps health on pickup of normal/rotten.

mechanics.name: max_health_with_megahealth
mechanics.notes: megahealth allows health > max_health up to 250 then decays.

mechanics.name: start_health
mechanics.notes: standard DM starting health.

mechanics.name: start_weapon_default
mechanics.notes: parm1 = IT_SHOTGUN | IT_AXE (both items granted via bitmask OR on the same line).

mechanics.name: view_offset_z
mechanics.notes: eye height. Engine-side really; surfaced in QC default but often considered engine constant.

mechanics.name: pent_invulnerability_mechanic
mechanics.notes: implementation is full damage absorb (not partial). The protect3 hit sound is throttled to once every 2 seconds (combat.qc:189) so rapid-fire weapons do not replay it every frame.

mechanics.name: quad_damage_multiplier
mechanics.notes: door damage is NOT quaded. combat.qc:127 is the if(deathmatch==4) gate; line 128 is the *8 path; line 130 is the default *4 path.

mechanics.name: ring_invisibility_mechanic
mechanics.notes: client modelindex swap; partial visibility threshold is engine-side. While the ring is active the player skips pain animation frames (player.qc:348, "eyes don't have pain frames") -- a subtle tell that a ringed player takes hits without flinching.

mechanics.name: inter_level_carry_over
mechanics.notes: SetChangeParms normalizes the player's state when carrying between single-player levels: health is clamped to [50, 100] (client.qc:49/51) and shells are floored to 25 (client.qc:56), so you never enter the next map below 50 health or 25 shells. Other ammo, items and armor carry as-is.

mechanics.name: intermission_exit_delay
mechanics.notes: 5-second wait after intermission before any player can advance.

mechanics.name: respawn_button_press
mechanics.notes: id1 respawn requires +attack/+jump press; no auto-respawn timer.

mechanics.name: spawn_clearance_radius
mechanics.notes: SelectSpawnPoint uses findradius(spot.origin, 84) to count players near each candidate spawn; spots with no one inside 84 units form the preferred pool, and when all are occupied the algorithm falls back to a random spot.

mechanics.name: spawn_invul_default
mechanics.notes: no spawn invul in DM<=3. Line 470 in client.qc is invisible_finished=0; line 471 is invincible_finished=0.

mechanics.name: spawn_invul_dm4
mechanics.notes: 3-second invul on spawn in OctaPower mode.

mechanics.name: spawn_invul_dm5
mechanics.notes: 3-second invul on spawn in Quadmachine mode.

mechanics.name: bloodfest_boss_damage_amplifier
mechanics.notes: In bloodfest the boss player's outgoing damage is multiplied by 4 (`damage *= 4` at combat.c:535, gated `k_bloodfest && attacker->bloodfest_boss`). Mechanic constant, NOT a monster entity row -- disjoint from the bloodfest monster keyspace. Mode-scoped (niche co-op mode).

props.requires: attacker->bloodfest_boss is set (the bloodfest boss player)

mechanics.name: bloodfest_shambler_full_explosion_damage
mechanics.notes: In bloodfest a shambler takes full (not half) rocket/grenade explosion damage, because the half-damage guard at combat.c:1219 is disabled when k_bloodfest is set. Mechanic constant, not a monster row. Mode-scoped.

props.mechanism: the shambler half-damage guard is `!cvar(k_bloodfest)`-gated, so it is disabled in bloodfest (combat.c:1219)
props.ktx_bloodfest_value: 1.0x (full explosion damage -- the half-damage resistance is removed)

mechanics.name: ctf_resistance_rune_damage_reduction
mechanics.notes: CTF resistance rune divides a target's incoming damage by a k_ctf_rune_power_res factor (combat.c:556). Mode-scoped.

props.requires: target holds the CTF resistance rune (ctf_flag & CTF_RUNE_RES)

mechanics.name: ctf_strength_rune_damage_boost
mechanics.notes: CTF strength rune scales an attacker's outgoing damage by a k_ctf_rune_power_str factor (combat.c:550). Gate {"mode":"ctf"}; the rune is a runtime player flag and the multiplier is cvar-tunable (props). Mode-scoped.

props.requires: attacker holds the CTF strength rune (ctf_flag & CTF_RUNE_STR)

mechanics.name: instagib_player_hit_damage
mechanics.notes: In instagib, any player-originated hit deals 5000 (`take = 5000` at combat.c:715), a one-shot kill. Self-hits are zeroed. Mode-scoped.

props.condition: inflictor->ct == ctPlayer (any player-originated hit); self-hits are zeroed (combat.c:717)

mechanics.name: lg_water_discharge_damage_per_cell
mechanics.notes: KTX gates the lightning-gun water-discharge radius damage behind the k_dis cvar. With the default k_dis=0 the discharge deals no radius damage (weapons.c:1202); with k_dis==2 out-of-water targets are spared (combat.c:1196). Cvar-gated (D22); the value-specific condition (k_dis==2) is in props per the single-key rule.

props.id1_value: 35 * cells radius damage, applied to all targets in radius
props.ktx_facet_a: the LG water-discharge radius explosion is suppressed unless k_dis != 0 (default k_dis=0 -> no radius damage at all)
props.ktx_facet_b: with k_dis == 2, out-of-water non-self targets take 0 from the discharge (dtLG_DIS)

mechanics.name: midair_no_self_rl_damage
mechanics.notes: In midair a player takes no self rocket damage (`take = 0` at combat.c:707), where vanilla applies halved self-splash. Mode-scoped.

mechanics.name: midair_rl_airborne_instakill
mechanics.notes: Midair's core rule: a rocket hitting a sufficiently-airborne player deals 9999 (instant kill) -- `take = 9999` at combat.c:686, with the height guards immediately below. Mode-scoped.

props.condition: target is a player hit by a rocket (rl_dmg) and airborne (playerheight >= midair_minheight and >= 45)

mechanics.name: yawnmode_grenade_deterministic_aim
mechanics.notes: Yawnmode removes random scatter from the grenade launch angle (`if (k_yawnmode) { r1 = r2 = 0; }` at weapons.c:1412), making grenade aim fully deterministic. Mode-scoped.

props.id1_value: crandom() scatter offsets on the launch angle

mechanics.name: yawnmode_lg_water_discharge_self_kill
mechanics.notes: In dmm4+ (weapons.c:1185), firing the lightning gun underwater normally has a 50% self-kill chance; yawnmode makes it always self-kill for 4000 (`if (k_yawnmode || g_random() <= 0.5) T_Damage(self,..,4000)` at weapons.c:1189-1192). Mode-scoped (+ dmm4+).

props.id1_value: 50% chance to self-kill when discharging underwater in dmm4+
props.ktx_value: 100% self-kill (4000 damage) when yawnmode is active

mechanics.name: yawnmode_nail_knockback
mechanics.notes: Yawnmode increases nail knockback 20% (`nailkick = 1.2` at combat.c:904, gated `k_yawnmode && inflictor->classname == "spike"` at combat.c:902). Mode-scoped.

mechanics.name: yawnmode_shotgun_deterministic_spread
mechanics.notes: In yawnmode the shotgun family (SG + SSG, all routed through FireBullets) places pellets on a fixed deterministic grid instead of random scatter (`non_random_bullets = k_yawnmode || ...` at weapons.c:550). The visible consequence (operator SME note): because pellets group predictably, you keep effective shotgun damage at range, where vanilla's random spread drops pellets. Distinct from the k_classic_shotgun cvar, which only changes the gunshot-puff effect grouping (cosmetic, not cataloged). Mode-scoped (or via the 'nrb' practice toggle outside matches).

props.id1_value: per-pellet random spread (crandom() * spread on right/up axes), identical to vanilla
props.ktx_value: fixed deterministic pellet grid (the non_random_bullets ladder in FireBullets)
props.effective_impact: deterministic pellets land predictably, so shotgun/SSG connect reliably at range -- vanilla random scatter loses pellets at distance, KTX yawnmode does not
props.nrb_practice_path: also active via the 'nrb' userinfo key when not in a match (weapons.c:551)

mechanics.name: quad_damage_multiplier
mechanics.notes: In midair, quad damage does not multiply outgoing damage at all -- the quad-damage block is suppressed by the `!midair` condition (combat.c:540). Quad in midair only makes rockets fast (see the rocket midair row). Mode-scoped.

props.id1_value: 4x outgoing damage while quad active (dmm4 OctaPower 8x)
props.ktx_midair_value: 1x -- quad does NOT multiply damage in midair (it only speeds rockets)
